text:
jane-cs: FYI a large customer is seeing a spike of 429s right after we pushed the new per-key rate policy this morning. They're hitting it hard on embeddings and realtime generation. Customer says it started ~20m after the deploy.
asha-support: ugh. do we know which policy rolled? region? any correlation id from their logs?
simon-engineering: looks like the canary for the ratecap change rolled to 25% globally at ~1769876400. targeted routing rule was supposed to be traffic: 10% canary; somehow the percentage param was wrong in the push. I'm pulling the rollout job now.
lee-sre: can you paste the rollout job id? i want to check autoscaler logs, might be a batching/queue backpressure interaction causing token spikes -> 429s.
simon-engineering: job id rdo-2026-03-15-09A. here is the commit diff we applied: ```yaml
rate_limits:
  default_per_key: 60rps
  burst_window_ms: 500
  canary:
    enabled: true
    percentage: 25  # should have been 10
    scope: global
```
maria-product: why was percentage 25? I thought QA confirmed 10 in the PR.
asha-support: customer says they started getting 429s on embedding endpoints and then on text-generation. They provided example curl and a sample response: ```json
{"error":"rate_limit_exceeded","code":429,"message":"quota exhausted for key foo-XXX"}
```
lee-sre: checking region metrics now. ops-bot: metrics link -> https://redwood.internal/monitoring/rl/1769876400 (CPU/rt/429s). We see a sudden jump in 429s aligned with the rollout.
ash-support: can we roll back to previous policy immediately and then re-roll with proper canary?
simon-engineering: yes. rollback plan: 1) halt rollout, 2) revert to policy v12 (prev config), 3) re-run with percentage=10 and add gating on 429 rate < 0.5% over 5m windows. I can push the revert now.
deploy-bot: deploy rdo-2026-03-15-09A paused by simon-engineering at 1769876555 :thumbsup:
simon-engineering: performing revert: ```bash
redwoodctl policy apply --policy-id rl-policy-2026 --file rl-policy-v12.yaml --region all
```
deploy-bot: policy rl-policy-2026 reverted to v12 by simon-engineering at 1769876578. rollout percentage set to 0%.
asha-support: customer noticed a partial improvement ~2m after revert, but they still have residual 429s from queued requests. i told them to retry with exponential backoff and that we are investigating.
lee-sre: We should also add a temporary allowlist for that customer's org id to prevent further impact while we re-roll. simon, can you add an override rule scoped to org: cust-981?
simon-engineering: adding override now: ```yaml
overrides:
  - matcher: org == "cust-981"
    rate_limit: 120rps
    burst_window_ms: 1000
```
deploy-bot: override rule applied at 1769876622.
maria-product: next steps: - postmortem after stabilization - add automated guard in rollout tool that prevents >15% canary unless explicit opt-in - require canary gating on 429 and latency signals.
oncall-rotation: recommend paging eng-sre if 429 rate doesn't fall below 0.5% in the next 10m.
simon-engineering: re-roll into canary with corrected percentage and gating: ```bash
redwoodctl policy rollout --policy rl-policy-2026 --canary 10 --gate "429_rate < 0.005 over 5m" --strategy gradual
```
simon-engineering: starting gradual canary at 1769876680. will monitor.
lee-sre: watching dashboards + adding temporary qps smoothing at the ingress (token bucket tweak) to reduce bursts. i set burst_window to 800ms cluster-wide for the next 30m.
asha-support: customer is asking for ETA. i told them we reverted and applied an override; canary is being re-run at 10% with backoff gating. gave ETA 30-45m for confirmation.
simon-engineering: update: at +4m canary at 10% shows no abnormal 429s, latency stable. proceeding with staged ramp every 10m +10% with gate checks.
deploy-bot: canary monitor: 10% -> ok; next increment scheduled in 10m.
lee-sre: leaving the org override in place for 2h post full rollout, then we remove.
maria-product: excellent. please capture exact timeline and all config diffs for the postmortem. also open a ticket to add a lint to the rollout job preventing accidental percentage typos.
asha-support: logging the customer's case number CS-99321 and will follow up once fully resolved. thanks everyone for the fast turnaround :pray:
jane-cs: +1 customer emailed back thanking the quick response; they want the follow-up summary and the planned changes. i'll draft the customer note after we have full postmortem.
